title: Proximity resize rail with filter peek and density meter
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Our virtualized table currently exposes a blunt column-resize affordance that is hard to hit on high-density rows and on small screens; it also interrupts pointer-based filtering flows because users must switch to the header to open filter menus. Goal: introduce a proximity-aware resize rail (thin interaction zone that appears when pointer nears a column boundary) plus an inline filter peek UI and a lightweight density meter to make density mode discovery explicit. This ticket covers design specs, accessibility requirements, interaction animations, edge cases with virtualization (sticky headers, overscan), and handoff tokens to engineering and PM.

Acceptance criteria (high-level):
- Proximity resize rail appears within 12px of column boundary on hover/focus and expands to a 10px hit area for drag.
- Resize rail supports keyboard focus and arrow-based incremental resize with 1px steps; SHIFT+arrow for 10px steps.
- When a column header has an active filter, a compact filter-peek chip should appear on hover next to the column title showing the number of active predicates and allow one-click open of the full filter panel.
- Density meter (tiny slider with 3 presets: Comfortable, Compact, Dense) visible in table toolbar and in a condensed header overflow; updating density updates row height tokens and recomputes visible rows without breaking virtualization.
- All interactions meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast and keyboard operability; automated axe checks pass for the header interactions.
- Figma components, tokens, and a short interaction spec are uploaded and linked; engineering has a clear mapping of tokens to CSS variables and runtime props.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Proximity rail vs always-visible drag handle: proximity reduces visual clutter on large tables but needs careful hover intent handling to avoid flicker during fast drags. We debounce appearance by 80ms and use a 150ms hide delay.
- For virtualization, we will render a lightweight pseudo-rail in the DOM outside the visible cell content to avoid reflow costs; engineering to validate that this approach doesn't introduce extra layout thrash with overscan.
- The filter peek intentionally shows only a concise summary (count + short label). Full predicate editing remains in the existing filter panel to avoid duplicating complex UI.
- Density changes should not reinitialize column widths. We will test two strategies: (A) scale row padding tokens only, (B) adjust font-size token for compact view — prefer (A) to avoid layout cascades.

Deliverables:
- Annotated Figma file with component variants and interaction flows (hover, focus, drag, keyboard).
- Accessibility checklist and keyboard spec.
- Example usage snippets for console table and for small-card table variant.
- Engineering acceptance criteria and QA checklist.

Out of scope: column grouping reflow, column pinning UX changes, server-side sorting implementation (frontend filter/sort UX only).
